Formulation
- Summary: Patient presents with a recent (≈6-week) left-sided hearing deterioration with intermittent tinnitus and milder non-rotatory dizziness. A similar transient episode occurred ~1 year prior. No ear pain, discharge, or fever reported. Possible reversible causes to exclude include impacted cerumen/wax or middle ear pathology; if external/middle ear causes excluded, further evaluation of inner ear/balance system may be required. Factors contributing: prior transient episode (predisposing), unknown trigger (precipitating), use of cotton buds (patient acknowledged cleaning ears with cotton buds — may perpetuate impaction), and ongoing tinnitus symptoms. Protective factors include patient engagement and agreement to follow-up and education.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Left-sided hearing deterioration (≈6 weeks)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Attend face-to-face clinic for ear examination within the next 4–5 days
  - Understand likely causes and next steps
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Exclude external/middle ear causes (e.g., impacted wax) and identify any treatable pathology
  - Provide appropriate management (wax removal or onward referral) based on findings
- Actions (Patient):
  - Contact support/admin team (per clinician instruction) to be slotted into face-to-face clinic within ~4–5 days
  - Avoid using cotton buds in the ear
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Place instructions in notes and request admin to book patient into an in-person clinic within ~4–5 days
  - Examine ear (otoscopy) at face-to-face appointment and manage/remove wax if present or refer as indicated
  - If ear is clear, consider further assessment/referral for middle/inner ear or balance system evaluation

Secondary Problem: Left-sided tinnitus
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Receive information about tinnitus and understand management options
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide education about tinnitus and discuss limited treatment options; integrate findings from ear examination into tinnitus management
- Actions (Patient):
  - Read provided tinnitus information leaflet (link to be placed in notes)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Paste tinnitus information leaflet link into appointment notes
  - Review tinnitus information with patient at clinic visit and proceed with management based on ear exam results

Tertiary Problem: Intermittent dizziness/imbalance (non-vertiginous)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Have dizziness assessed in context of ear exam and management
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Determine whether dizziness is related to middle/inner ear pathology and arrange appropriate follow-up or referral
- Actions (Patient):
  - Report severity and characteristics of dizziness during face-to-face assessment; seek earlier review if symptoms worsen
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Assess dizziness during ear examination; if indicated, investigate vestibular causes or refer to ENT/audiology or balance clinic

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Explanation of tinnitus (limited understanding in medicine), advice to avoid cotton buds, plan for ear examination, and provision of a tinnitus information leaflet (link to be placed in notes)
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Not recorded (patient advised to rebook if any problems or worsening before clinic)
- Coping Strategies: Not recorded (patient directed to read leaflet for information about tinnitus)
